column2: robot_otak.ino: for the ESP32-S3 (board: ESP32S3 Dev Module, PSRAM OPI, 16M Flash (3MB APP/9.9MB FATFS)).

If the MPU6050 is already fitted (Step 6), type T 90: the wheels spin as for a right turn. Because the robot is lifted, the gyroscope feels no rotation, so after about 4 seconds the wheels stop on their own and E PUTAR_GAGAL appears with a small number. That is correct. On the floor (Part 6) the robot stops after exactly 90° and replies OK T 90. At power-on, keep the DevKit still for about 1 second: the Serial Monitor prints Bias giroskop, normally below 5.

Why does it work this way? The D line holds front distance, rear distance, battery, temperature, humidity, pitch, roll, flag, and turn rate (degrees per second). The brain reads the same line over UART every 250 ms. Every movement stops on its own when its time runs out (max 3 seconds), so if the brain hangs or the UART wire comes loose, the robot does not run away.
The body obeys commands and refuses dangerous moves. Every second the Serial Monitor shows a data line such as D 45 120 7.92 29.5 70 1 -2 0 0.
16M Flash (3MB APP/9.9MB FATFS) (two code slots, needed for uploading over WiFi later)
Can be made permanent The Arduino Tools settings (OPI PSRAM, 3MB APP partition) and the S3 staying plugged into its expansion board: both go up to level 3 as one unit.

Weather comes free from Open-Meteo, no key needed. Fill in CUACA_KOTA, CUACA_LAT, and CUACA_LON with your location: in Google Maps right-click your home, the first number is latitude (LAT), the second is longitude (LON). The default is Mataram.

Make sure the body runs the latest robot_badan.ino (it has the T command for precise gyro turns). If your body code is older, upload it again once over USB and fill in your BATERAI_FAKTOR again. Every time you switch on, keep the robot still for about 1 second: the body measures the gyroscope while still.
Set Tools as in Part 3 Step 1 (PSRAM: OPI PSRAM, Partition Scheme: 16M Flash (3MB APP/9.9MB FATFS)). The first upload must go over the USB cable. The first compile can take a few minutes.

Later uploads can go over WiFi without taking the robot apart: laptop and robot on the same WiFi, open Tools → Port, pick the network port zond at 10.x.x.x, then Upload as usual. The screen shows the progress; do not switch the robot off. Fill in OTA_SANDI if you do not want others on the same WiFi to be able to replace the code (Arduino IDE asks for it when uploading).
The full code is about 2,200 lines (mostly the compressed web panel): download robot_otak.ino. Do not upload a file that already contains your token and API keys anywhere public.
Sketch too big error, or WiFi upload refused: Partition Scheme is not 3MB APP yet. Change it, then upload once over USB.

Network port does not appear under Tools → Port: wait about 1 minute after the robot starts, close and reopen Arduino IDE, or upload over USB. A WiFi upload that fails halfway does no harm: the old code keeps running.
Web panel or Telegram: /belok 90, /belok -90, /balik
the robot spins in place exactly 90° right, 90° left, or 180°, measured by the MPU6050 gyroscope. The AI uses it too when you say "turn around"
Telegram: /cuaca
temperature, chance of rain, and today's weather from Open-Meteo. A short version shows on the screen next to the date, and is added to reminders before 11 am
Telegram: /alarm 06:30 berangkat kerja, /alarm harian 04:30 sholat subuh, /alarm, /alarm hapus 2

one-time or daily reminders (up to 12): the robot speaks the message and sends it to Telegram. In the web panel (Alarm and reminders section) you can also pick specific days and an extra sound: radio or a song from the SD card. Prayer times are entered by hand one by one. Also works through the AI: "remind me at 7 to leave for work"
Just leave it
the expression changes by itself: sleepy between 22:00 and 05:00 after 2 minutes unused, weak when the battery is low, surprised when lifted, dizzy when spun around by hand
Web panel: tick Fitur kamera AI, then Lihat sekeliling (or /sekeliling)

the head turns left, front, and right, takes a photo in each direction, then the AI describes the surroundings over Telegram. Off by default because each run uses the AI with 3 photos (the AI quota runs out faster)
Web panel: Main suit (or /suit), after ticking Fitur kamera AI

the robot says "Suit! Batu, gunting, kertas!" (rock, paper, scissors) and takes a photo right after "kertas". Show your hand 30-50 cm in front of the camera before the sentence ends. The AI guesses your hand, the robot announces the winner and the score

/belok replies "Badan belum punya giroskop": the body code is still the old version, so the robot turns by time (less accurate). Upload robot_badan.ino again. Replies "Roda selip atau macet": slippery floor, thick carpet, or low battery.

Rock-paper-scissors often says "tanganmu tidak terlihat jelas" (hand not clear): the room is too dark, or the hand is too far or shown too late. Check the camera image in the web panel to make sure your hand is in the frame.

Send /belok 90 then /balik: the robot turns exactly a quarter then half a turn, measured by the gyroscope. If it always overshoots by a few degrees, increase 0.06f in updateGyro in the body code (stops earlier); if it always falls short, decrease it.
